## F1 [A10 / brief 4: factor names another factor] enroll_ext_payment_plan_installment, factor meal_status_extra_installment (rule l.2208, compute_basis me_status/extra_installments l.2273-2275)
Quote: "A family whose child's meal account in status active holds any Free Meal Status tier has the plan spread over free_extra more installments than the plan-length schedule gives, one whose child's meal account holds any Reduced-Price Meal Status tier over reduced_extra more, and any other family over none more."
The factor's only defining sentence names another declared factor (plan_length_schedule). Its factor document can't carry it verbatim, and any rewording ("more than the plan otherwise has") would be rendering around the defect. Compare the household-size sentence in the same rule ("has the plan spread over hh_three_extra more installments"), which names no other factor. The assembly sentence "then the number of installments is fixed" doesn't say how the counts combine (compute: plan_count + extra_installments + hh_extra, l.2255). Fix direction: drop "than the plan-length schedule gives" and say in the generic order sentence that the installment counts are added together.

## F2 [A2 / A10: plain sentence names a factor] enroll_ext_late_fee_transition_waiver, plain binding wv_fee (rule l.2025, compute_basis wv_fee l.2068-2069)
Quote: "... part of the late fee posted for that billing month is waived by a credit against that late fee with credit_reason billing_correction, and the waiver is never more than the part of the late fee the standing-part rule gives."
wv_fee is a non-factor binding, so its basis sentence belongs to the computation document. That sentence names the declared factor standing_part_rule ("the standing-part rule gives") and defines the limit through it. The computation document has to be silent about factors (and the baseline limit is the whole late fee, waiver_base baseline = sp_fee). Fix direction: state the limit in the plain sentence generically ("never more than the late fee") and leave "the part still standing after credits" to the standing-part sentence alone.

## F3 [A9 / B1: one grouping, edge on the tree path] enroll_ext_payment_plan_installment, factor down_payment_terms (rule l.2208; compute down_payment l.2240-2241)
Quote: "Under the down-payment rule, an enrollment carrying two or more late fees in the school year pays down_payment_pct percent of the open balance as a down payment in the first installment before the rest is divided, one carrying exactly one late fee pays that late fee as the down payment, and one carrying none pays no down payment."
Compute takes the late fee as posted: SUM(amount, event_type='enroll_tuition_late_fee', billing_month=LATEST late-fee month), gross of any credit. This policy's prerequisite chain (reversal, then waiver) posts credits against exactly that late fee. So with one late fee, "pays that late fee" has two natural readings: the fee as posted (what compute does) or the part of it still owing after the reversal and waiver credits. The two give different down payments. Fix direction: pin the amount in the rule ("the amount of that late fee as posted, whatever credits stand against it", or the net part, matching compute).

## F4 [B7 / A9: rule word with no record mapping] enroll_ext_eligibility_month_credit, factor basis_month_convention (rule l.1681; compute credited_tuition l.1698-1699, scope_status/added l.1708-1710)
Quote: "a free or reduced-price status from a household application that took effect no later than day half_month_start_day less one of the basis month has the whole month's tuition credited ...; a status from Direct Certification or a categorical designation is credited by calendar days ...; and a child without such a status in the basis month has nothing credited."
The records hold meal tiers, not a "source". Compute puts 'Free Meal Status (Household Application)' and 'Reduced-Price Meal Status' in the household-application branch, and 'Free Meal Status (Direct Certification)' and 'Free Meal Status (Categorical Eligibility)' in the calendar-day branch. It gives 'Free Meal Status (Prior-Year Carryover)' and 'Reduced-Price Meal Status (Prior-Year Carryover)' nothing credited, while still treating them as in scope (additions apply, l.1710). A carryover status rests on the prior year's determination, often a household application, so a reader can't tell whether a carryover tier gets the whole/half-month method or nothing. The rule never names the tiers. Fix direction: name the tiers for each branch, carryover tiers included, as policy 7 does ("any Free Meal Status tier").

## F5 [rule vs compute wording] enroll_ext_late_fee_share_reversal (rule l.1845; factor credited_share_reversal ladder l.1928-1929; tool credit_prek_late_fee_reversal_2a81de73 docstring)
Quote (rule, first sentence): "When the most recent billing month's tuition charge carries an eligibility credit, the late fee posted for that billing month is partly reversed by a credit against the late fee with credit_reason eligibility_established."
Quote (same rule): "when the eligibility credits standing against the most recent billing month's tuition charge equal or exceed that charge the whole late fee is reversed"
Quote (tool docstring): "Post the reversal of part of a Pre-K tuition late fee ..."
The policy can reverse the whole late fee: the full-credit tier, or additions capped at the fee (limited = MN(rv_fee, added), l.1888). "Partly reversed" / "reversal of part" says a full reversal can't happen. Fix direction: "is reversed in whole or in part" in both places.

## F6 [A3 / A4: shared definition lives only in a factor sentence] enroll_ext_late_fee_assessment, plain lf_owed vs factor unpaid_month_schedule (rule l.996; compute lf_owed l.1026, um_part l.1016-1017)
Quote (plain lf_owed basis): "A billing month that already carries a late fee, none of whose tuition is still unpaid on the day the fee is assessed, or whose due day is fewer than tuition_late_fee_offset_days days before that day, owes no late fee, additions included."
Quote (factor sentence, the only definition): "Under the unpaid-month schedule, the part of the month's tuition still unpaid is the lesser of that month's tuition charge and the open balance (the enrollment's tuition charges, late fees and refunds less its payments and credits, payments reaching the oldest open charge first): ..."
lf_owed (non-factor) uses the same quantity, MN(month charge, MX(0, open balance)) > 0. The only definition of it, including the open-balance definition, sits inside the unpaid-month schedule's factor sentence. A reader of the computation document alone has no definition of "still unpaid". Fix direction: define "the part of the month's tuition still unpaid" (and the open balance) once in a plain sentence, and let the schedule sentence use it.

## F7 [B1 month-end] enroll_ext_eligibility_month_credit, factor basis_month_convention (compute credited_tuition l.1699)
Compute: household-application branch gives half when `bc_offset < 31`. The calendar-day branch gives tuition × MX(0, month_days_convention − bc_offset) ÷ month_days_convention, with bc_offset = days from the 1st of the basis month to the status effective date.
Rule: "... one that took effect on or after day half_month_start_day has half of it credited; ... and a child without such a status in the basis month has nothing credited."
For a status that takes effect after the basis month ends, in a month shorter than 31 days, compute still credits where the rule credits nothing. Example: basis month November, effective December 1 → offset 30 → half. Example: basis month February, effective March 1 → offset 28 → half, or 2/30 by calendar days. This is only reachable when the most recent charged month comes before the status month (the next month's charge not posted), so it is low-reach, but it is a rule/compute disagreement at a month end. Fix direction: test "effective date within the basis month" by the month itself, not by a 31-day offset.
